answer: Each reputation contribution decays exponentially with a defined half-life, so influence requires sustained, recent honest service rather than a one-time score. In the EigenTrust-style matrix, a freshly spawned sybil has near-zero eigenvector centrality without trusted, reciprocal paths; temporal decay and reciprocity-weighted transitivity make bootstrapping costly, while consensus thresholds reject unsupported influence. A beacon may flag collusion; lotus and island identities remain untrusted until verified through service.
